items.title: 'The president loves Stephen': The man by Trump's side changing America
items.description: From a young age, Stephen Miller was campaigning for ideas that were extremely conservative and extremely strange for a teenager from California. Now, he's running Donald Trump's immigration agenda.

items.title: Why the backyard sprinkler is on the climate change frontline
items.description: Billions of litres of water are sprayed onto household gardens every day during summer, allowing cities to stay green. Now water is running low. Has the sprinkler had its day?

items.title: 'We will be recognised': 21-year-old Australian backs his micronation
items.description: Daniel Jackson claims to be the youngest president in the world. The problem is that no other countries recognise him.

items.title: Liberal frontbenchers dismiss prospect of imminent leadership challenge
items.description: Shadow treasurer Ted O'Brien says it is his "assumption" that Liberal frontbencher Angus Taylor still supports Sussan Ley, despite days of speculation that he's planning to challenge for the leadership.

items.title: 'A really big threat': US territories brace for Trump's deep sea mining
items.description: A Trump administration push to begin deep-sea mining is gathering momentum — and stirring alarm in United States Pacific territories.

items.title: Starmer calls for Andrew to testify as new details about Epstein friendship revealed
items.description: The royal family faces a fresh round of embarrassment after the latest tranche of Epstein files revealed unsavoury details about the convicted sex offender's relationship with Andrew.

items.title: A GP refused to give Claire weight-loss drugs — but Juniper approved them
items.description: Claire Munch says she was hospitalised with an eating disorder after a telehealth provider approved weight-loss drugs her GP had refused — and that even after she complained, she was later sent marketing promotions.

items.title: Olympian Michael Klim warned his fiancée she'd met the 'dud version' of him
items.description: Olympian Michael Klim forged his reputation on strength and athleticism. But after being blindsided by an incurable muscle-wasting disease, he was forced to reinvent himself.

items.title: 'Brave' 12yo shark attack victim honoured with paddle-out at North Bondi
items.description: Hundreds of paddle boarders and others journey into the waves of North Bondi to pay tribute to 12-year-old shark victim Nico Antic.

items.title: US judge orders 5-year-old and father be released from ICE detention
items.description: A US judge orders a five-year-old boy and his father to be released from immigration detention after their arrest in Minnesota last month.

items.title: What 50C summers will mean for Australia — and why they're more likely
items.description: Heatwaves are becoming longer, more frequent and more intense with multiple days of 50C looking more likely.

items.title: Alcaraz, Djokovic meet in Australian Open battle of generational greats
items.description: More tennis history will go on the line when Novak Djokovic and Carlos Alcaraz clash in an Australian Open final of the highest stakes.

items.title: Every day is a 'disgusting lucky dip', say op shop volunteers
items.description: A regional op shop donation infested with bed bugs shocks one country Victorian town — but not some op shop volunteers.

items.title: Victoria is flipping 'the big switch' on its Metro Tunnel. Here's what is changing
items.description: New timetables are being rolled out across Melbourne's train network, with more than 1,200 extra weekly services commencing from today.

items.title: Cinephile hopes knowledge of slashers will help her escape horror speed dating event
items.description: Debut author Shailee Thompson's new novel How to Kill a Guy in Ten Dates follows cinephile Jamie Prescott, who has to rely on her extensive knowledge of what not to do in a slasher situation when a speed-dating event she attends turns deadly.

items.title: How to unlock your home's history with patience and a little detective work
items.description: When Billy Harraway-Jones dug into the history of his family home, he discovered a saga of courtship and marriage in a new world, and of life and death on the Australian goldfields.

items.title: Chia seed challenge part of the online 'wellness loop'
items.description: The health benefits of chia seeds have been well publicised, but health and internet experts are urging people to not believe everything you see on social media.

items.title: How Celia Pacquola went from Bluey disappointment to Dog Park Delight
items.description: In the new cathartic drama/comedy starring Leon Ford and Celia Pacquola, dogs are the answer to everything.

items.title: Timbertown living museum closes after almost half a century
items.description: Thousands of tourists and students on school excursions passed through the doors of the heritage village to get an idea of what life was like for Australia's colonial-era timber-getters.

items.title: Thousands rally to show support after alleged rape of runner in Rockhampton
items.description: The Rockhampton community comes together in a show of emotional support after a young woman was allegedly sexually assaulted and nearly drowned by a stranger on a walking track.

items.title: 'Not a house, it's a home': Public housing tenants' human rights breached
items.description: An ACT Supreme Court judge quotes from Cicero and the movie The Castle, as she rules in favour of three Canberra public housing tenants who claimed plans to move them breached their human rights.

items.title: Workers allege exploitation on Ningaloo Reef tour boats
items.description: Tourists pay top dollar to see one of Australia's most pristine coral reefs, but those working on the boats say they are being taken advantage of.

items.title: Four recipes to help solve your lunch box problems
items.description: As kids head back into classrooms, we've put together some recipes to help their school lunch boxes come home empty.

items.title: Come on trivia titans, it's time to show me what you've got
items.description: I love that you just keep coming back for more humiliating defeat.

items.title: How a copy of a stolen ancient vase ended up on a grand slam podium
items.description: Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic go head-to-head today in the men's singles final. Not many people know they are competing for a trophy based on an Ancient Roman artefact.
